dataset.description: In this dataset, the obtained results of Active-Dynamic Thermography maneuvers, including feedback-guided skin cooling in patients with sepsis. Obtained data are series of FLIR thermal images of upper legs before and after skin cooling under controlled conditions.

distribution.title: The proposed technique integrates active dynamic thermography and narrow-band imaging, offering non-invasive, real-time evaluation of microcirculatory perfusion for sepsis patient phenotyping. The project develops a multimodal, non-contact optical method for personalised hemodynamic phenotyping of skin microcirculation. Active dynamic thermography (ADT) characterises the functional density, perfusion and spatial distribution of cutaneous perforator arteries, while narrow-band imaging (NBI) quantifies mottling as the spatial distribution and dynamics of total haemoglobin associated with venous stagnation. Combining these markers is intended to distinguish four provisional physiological phenotypes: excessive arteriolar vasoconstriction with venous stagnation (left-ventricular dysfunction); excessive vasoconstriction without venous stagnation (persistent hypovolaemia); absence of excessive vasoconstriction with venous stagnation (fluid overload); and absence of both (optimal resuscitation).
